questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the 'other half' of autoscaling that most teams never configure deliberately?
options: Scaling down aggressively when demand actually drops, instead of only scaling up for spikes
Switching the workload from on-demand to Reserved Instances automatically
Replacing the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler with a manual scaling process
Running the workload exclusively on Spot capacity at all times
questions.explain: Most autoscaling configurations only protect against traffic spikes. Using the same mechanism deliberately to scale down when demand drops is the cost-control half most teams skip.

questions.q: What distinguishes a workload that is a good fit for scale-to-zero from one that isn't?
options: Whether the workload runs on Kubernetes versus a VM scale set
Whether the workload is willing to tolerate a brief cold-start delay on the first request after idle
Whether the workload has ever been right-sized before
Whether the workload's maxReplicas setting is higher than 10
questions.explain: Scale-to-zero means no running instances at all until a request arrives. It only works for workloads where that cold-start delay is acceptable — never for anything a customer expects instantly available.

questions.q: What is the failure mode this lesson warns about when setting an autoscaler's minimum replica count too low?
options: The cloud provider will charge a penalty fee for a low minReplicas setting
A low minimum has no real downside as long as maxReplicas is high enough
A pod dying during a deploy or node drain can create a real availability gap while a replacement schedules, if the floor was set below what the system can gracefully recover from
Kubernetes will refuse to schedule any pods at all if minReplicas is set below 3
questions.explain: Scaling the minimum down past the point where the system can recover gracefully turns a cost win into a reliability gap during normal events like a deploy or node drain.

questions.q: This lesson recommends basing the off-hours minimum replica/instance count on what?
options: A fixed number copied from another team's configuration
Whatever the cloud provider's default minimum happens to be
The same real, observed low-traffic percentile utilization analysis used for right-sizing
The maximum traffic the workload has ever received, to stay safe
questions.explain: The off-hours minimum should come from real observed utilization data — the same percentile approach from the right-sizing lesson — not a guess.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend pairing a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler with a Cluster Autoscaler (or Karpenter)?
options: So that pod replicas never need to be scaled down at all
Because Kubernetes requires both to be installed before HPA will function
To disable scale-to-zero, which is considered unsafe on Kubernetes
So the underlying node capacity can shrink along with pod count, rather than paying for idle nodes with no pods running
questions.explain: Without a node-level autoscaler, scaling pods down can leave underlying VM nodes running idle — pairing HPA with a Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter lets the node count shrink too.
